title: Prefill Sentinel: graph stability and deferred kernel swap to ensure safe replay across streams
creator: Ava Chen
description: Introduce a lightweight runtime-level sentinel checkpoint written into CUDA graph captures and a deferred kernel swap mechanism to prevent inconsistent kernel/parameter states from causing nondeterministic replay failures when multiple decode streams interleave prefill and decode captures.
acceptance_criteria: Sentinel checkpoints are inserted at prefill boundary and validated at replay time for >99.9% of production capture paths without increasing median latency by >1%.

Deferred kernel swap prevents any replay that would mix incompatible kernel variants (quantized/packed/aligned variants) across CUDA graph segments; captured graphs that require incompatible kernels are atomically rejected and fall back to safe-mode decoding.
E2E canary on dedicated infra shows reduction in capture-induced replay failures by >=80% on a mixed workload (50% long-context prefill + 50% short prefill).
Runbook updated and Console alert created for sentinel mismatch events with trace links and suggested remediation steps.
design_notes: Problem: partial captures (interrupted prefill or in-flight kernel selection changes) can lead to replay inconsistencies when streams are interleaved or when kernel selection heuristics change mid-capture.

Core idea: on capture, runtime appends a small sentinel record to the CUDA graph metadata containing: (a) capture fingerprint (model/hash, batch shape, seq lens), (b) kernel-version table (selected kernel IDs and properties), (c) capture epoch id. On replay, the sentinel is validated and compared against the currently available kernels and stream epoch. If mismatch is detected, runtime will either (1) reject replay and route request to safe fallback decode with explicit telemetry OR (2) if mismatch is only kernel ordering, perform a deferred kernel swap before commit.

Deferred kernel swap: instead of immediately switching runtime-level kernel pointers during capture, we queue the swap and only apply it after all captures with older epoch have quiesced. Swaps carry a 'compatibility mask' so replay can decide to perform an atomic swap when safe, otherwise fallback.

Trade-offs: sentinel adds ~48-128 bytes per graph metadata and a small validation cost at replay. Deferred swaps add complexity to kernel lifecycle management and require quiesce detection; both are manageable compared to the cost of silent replay corruption.
decisions: Use compact 64-bit fingerprinting (siphash) rather than full SHA in metadata to reduce overhead (collision risk evaluated as negligible for our model set).
Fallback policy: nonblocking rejection + safe-mode decode for customer requests; flag as transient and auto-retry once runtime quiesces (can be tuned by policy).
Compatibility table will be maintained per-model in memory and persisted to agent state; it will include kernel property tags: quantization, alignment, occupancy-class, and ISA-bit requirements.
tasks: Implement sentinel emitter in capture path and attach to CUDA graph metadata (ENG runtime component).
Implement replay-time sentinel validator and compatibility checker.
Add deferred kernel swap coordinator with epoch tracking and quiesce detection hooks.
Extend telemetry: counters for sentinel_mismatch, deferred_swap_applied, replay_rejected, fallback_invocations.
Unit tests for sentinel encoding/decoding, simulated mismatch scenarios, and kernel swap race tests.
Integration: Canary job and workload in dedicated infra; observe for 7 days before progressive rollout.
Documentation: update runbook, Console alerting, and developer guide for kernel lifecycle.
